text:
jordan: Quick sync — final GA checklist sanity check. I pulled together what I think are the unresolved items: SLA numeric targets, docs/runbook owner, pricing bucket mapping, monitoring dashboards, and support escalation flow. Need owners and concrete deadlines.

maya: Thanks. Happy to own the runbook + playbook. Will need a little help from eng on exact error modes.

chris: For SLA numbers we should be conservative. I recommend: `p95 latency < 200ms` for hosted standard tier, `error rate < 0.5%` (5xx). Does that align with commercial expectations?

sam: That seems reasonable. For Dedicated we should call out throughput SLOs instead: `sustained 1000 req/min per pool` as a baseline for GA.

leo: On monitoring, I can add dashboards for latency/error tokens, plus per-model throughput. Can we decide which traces go to the 14-day vs 90-day retention? ops will push for 14-day by default.

tara: Pricing needs tie into SLA tiers. Commercial prefers one-page mapping: tier -> expected latency/throughput -> price multiplier. I'll draft a spreadsheet but need the SLOs locked.

jordan: Actionable: (1) Chris finalize SLA numbers by EOD Tue. (2) Maya own runbook and a concise one-pager by Thu. (3) Leo wire dashboards and confirm retention policy with Ops by Fri. (4) Tara produce pricing mapping draft once (1) lands. Sam verify Dedicated throughput wording.

chris: Quick question — do we want separate SLOs for streaming vs non-streaming paths? Streaming p95 is typically higher.

jordan: Good catch. Yes: separate SLOs. Add `streaming p95 < 500ms` for hosted standard. Please include that in your final doc.

maya: For the runbook I'll include these headings: symptoms, immediate mitigations, fallback model policies, rollback steps, and customer communication templates. Any other must-haves?

sam: Add KV-cache eviction behaviors and how to clear in stuck sessions. Also include a short checklist for Dedicated customers to validate capacity claims.

leo: Ops-bot: please post current retention/ingest cost estimate.

ops-bot: ingest-estimate: 14-day retention approx $2.8k/mo per 100k requests; 90-day approx $6.9k/mo (rough). Ping @leo for breakdown.

tara: FYI commercial asked for an exception path: customers who need 99.99% availability (higher SLA) should be flagged as "Enterprise Plus" — we should define what extra we require (runbook commitments, on-call rotation, and regional redundancy).

jordan: Let's not bake Enterprise Plus into GA — we'll document the exception path and the additional commitments. Tara: please sketch the Enterprise Plus checklist as an appendix.

chris: I'll include error budget burn reporting cadence and alert thresholds. Question for Maya: who is the escalation owner after L2?

maya: L3 oncall (eng-oncall rotation) for GA. I'll note the pager escalation chain and include sample pages.

jordan: Final ask — each owner, please put a single-line deliverable and a hard deadline in this thread by EOD today so I can convert to tickets.

chris: SLA numbers doc (p95 hosted <200ms, streaming p95 <500ms, error <0.5%) — deliverable posted — deadline: 2024-06-18 EOD.

maya: Runbook + one-pager (includes escalation chain) — deadline: 2024-06-20 COB.

leo: Dashboards + retention confirmation — deadline: 2024-06-21 noon.

tara: Pricing mapping draft + Enterprise Plus appendix — deadline: 2024-06-21 EOD.

sam: Dedicated throughput wording + capacity checklist — deadline: 2024-06-20 EOD.

jordan: Great — I'll make tickets and assign. If anyone thinks a deadline is unrealistic, flag now. Otherwise I'll close the loop after tickets are up. :thumbsup:

leo: OK. I'll start the dashboard skeleton now.

maya: Starting runbook outline. Will ping eng for failure mode details.

chris: Will share SLA doc in PR and link here.

tara: I'll coordinate with commercial and share the pricing sheet.

sam: Copy — will validate Dedicated language.

jordan: Thanks all — keeping this lightweight so we can ship. We'll reconvene if any blocker pops up.
